new_entities.name: Vinpocetine
new_entities.description: A synthetic vincamine derivative marketed for cerebral blood flow and cognition.

new_entities.name: Cognitive function in vascular impairment
aliases: cognition in vascular dementia or hypoperfusion
new_entities.description: Cognitive performance in people with vascular cognitive impairment, vascular dementia, or chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.

edges.population: adults with vascular dementia, mixed dementia syndromes, or chronic cerebral hypoperfusion
edges.mechanism: Vinpocetine is mainly proposed to help by improving cerebrovascular reserve and modulating phosphodiesterase-dependent signaling in hypoperfused brain tissue. That vascular rationale is biologically plausible, but the clinical literature remains old, heterogeneous, and too inconsistent to show that better blood-flow physiology translates into dependable cognitive benefit.
edges.summary: Vinpocetine has shown occasional cognitive improvement signals in vascular or mixed dementia studies, but the evidence base remains inconclusive. The strongest review found only three old randomized trials, and later human work has been too heterogeneous or too small to turn vinpocetine into a convincing evidence-backed therapy for vascular cognitive decline.
edges.caveats: Much of this literature predates contemporary dementia trial standards, and several reports mix vascular and degenerative syndromes. Claims that vinpocetine is a proven cognition enhancer are much stronger than the actual human evidence supports.
